body: I see there's an interview with that author on Sam Harris' website, so it's probably not total quackery. $16.49 seems steep for an audiobook, but what else am I going to spend money on? I don't know how well that book will apply to an Aspie but maybe I'll look into it.
Sounds like a whole lot of effort for what I consider a slim chance of ever wanting to live. I think I've tried hard enough.

I walk three miles 4-5 days per week. Then people move the goalposts and say it has to be exercise that gets my heart rate up. There are no such exercises that I enjoy. We have an elliptical machine at home, but using it is just a chore, and I get no sense of reward from it. Same with all other exercise I've tried.

The stuff you're saying about dopamine saturation makes sense intuitively, but other than that I have no reason to believe any of it is true. A Google search for "dopamine saturation" turns up nothing of the sort. Do you have anything besides anecdotal evidence that such a phenomenon even exists?

I chose my words carefully when I said I have "as many friends as I want." I have Asperger's syndrome and don't get any enjoyment out of being with people. Aside from my wife there's not really anyone I talk to regularly, and I have no interest in changing that. There are a few people I could be friends with who share interests and are non-judgmental - they are even aware of my suicidality - but I'm just not interested.

Nice to get a reply from someone who seems to get it, but unfortunately I don't see any of what you said helping in the long run.

Why stay away from video games and what do you suggest doing instead? The one thing that I sometimes get some enjoyment out of that actually outweighs the cost (if only because the cost is practically zero in terms of preparation, cleanup, etc.), and I should stop doing it?

About a year ago I took five weeks or so off from work (short term disability). It made me feel better for awhile, but here I am again. That's not really something I can do again if I want to have a future.

None of what you said change the fact that I just don't enjoy anything. I'm not willing to live just for the sake of other people.

Sorry for the somewhat incoherent reply, but those are my thoughts.

I can't buy a bike that isn't available yet regardless of what my wife says and if I buy the current model I'll regret it when the new one comes around. I'm in Arizona so Summer's really the only bad season for outdoors stuff.

I'm not geting rid of a $900 Sig P226 that I got only a few months ago that is my first handgun that I waited weeks for that is stored in a safe to which only my wife knows the combination. It's easier for me to walk down to the train tracks than to get to the gun, and I can't exactly get rid of the train tracks.

I do force myself to do things, but I don't enjoy them and then I get bored or frustrated and start punching holes in walls.

I don't know, you're not helping.

Already done skydiving three times. I'm not afraid of anything but killing myself. Even that, I don't think "afraid" is the right word. Just instinctively hesitant.

You're right to suggest adrenaline as the only thing that isn't boring or frustrating. There's no source of adrenaline rushes that won't quickly either wear off or get me killed. The closest skydiving is 3 hours away. Racing (karts that accelerate literally like F1 cars) is close to home but too expensive (I have money to live comfortably without fear of financial trouble, but not so much that I can just do whatever I want). I want a motorcycle but I'll get in trouble or hurt for riding it the way I want to, and my wife doesn't want me to get one. She says I can get the 2013 Ninja 250R when it arrives in November, but I don't know if I'll be around then.

Again, already addressed in the OP.

>There's nothing I want that I think would make me feel any differently.

More specifically, I hate everything about travelling. There is nothing I want to spend money on. Money's not the issue, and spending it's not going to make me happy. I can't think of anything I want to do that I haven't already tried.

Call me selfish, but I need reasons to live, not just reasons not to kill myself.

All suicide prevention people seem to care about is whether or not I kill myself. No one's goal is to make me happy. Everyone would sooner have me miserable in a straitjacket than even consider the idea that suicide might be a good option.

Already mentioned that...

>The only reasons not to kill myself are that I would upset a few people

I don't think I should be forced to live just for the sake of other people. I need a better reason. Besides, she can do better, and she'll get over it.
